newsitem.title: USA: Saks decides against bidding for Barney's.
newsitem.headline: Saks decides against bidding for Barney's.

text.p: Saks Holdings Inc. said Monday it has decided not to bid for luxury retailer Barney's Inc., saying it could no longer justify its previous offer valued at about $290 million.
But it said it may be very interested in acquiring the retailer under different circumstances.

"We remain very interested in a potential purchase of Barney's under the appropriate conditions, and we expect to continue to work with Isetan" and other groups in the bankruptcy proceedings, Saks said in a statement.
Saks cited Barney's recent announcement of a substantial write-off and its decision last month to close several stores, including its original store on 17th Street in Manhattan.

Saks -- whose famed Fifth Avenue store predates Barney's as a luxury retailer -- said it remains interested in buying the upscale retailer, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in January 1996. In Chapter 11 a company is protected from its creditors as it tries to work out a plan to pay its debts.

Saks had teamed up with Japan's Isetan Co. Ltd. to buy Barney's for $290 million as part of a joint plan of reorganization. Other groups have bid for Barney's, including Hong Kong retailer Dickson Concepts Ltd., which has offered $240 million.
"We continue to believe that Saks is the most viable strategic buyer for Barney's, given our potential operating synergies, strong retailing management and understanding of the market," Saks said.
Saks made the announcement after stock markets closed. Its stock fell 19 cents to $23.44 Monday on the New York Stock Exchange.
